quest.title: Asipattravana Itihasa
quest.description: You need the help of the Pari Mihir and Rashnu to obtain the Chaplet. You might be able to find Mihir's trail in Asipattravana Swamp...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to Asipattravana Swamp to search for Mihir

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cold-hearted little Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon can't tell if you're genuinely scolding her or not!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: It is no difficult matter, saving Mihir. Perhaps I might even call it trivial. But we Pari each have our mission, and we also have different... ideals.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: She must've found some position equal in seclusion and defensibility, before using a Gray Gate to seal both the demons and herself in.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: If she could still move freely, aha, she would be like that Khvarena, begging for aid and prostrating herself before all and sundry to earn pity.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can Khvarena even prostrate themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe if they try hard enough?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: You plebeians miss the point. All the same, the state of this place tells me that she shall not hold out long by herself. How pitiful...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Pah, what a horrible sight. To be as Mihir is, corroded by filth, falling from a spotless to a sinful state, yet desperate to preserve herself... Had the Elder not bade me come...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. So after all that, you do care!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hardly! I merely wish to see if that useless fool has any regrets or not. If she turns back to us and accepts our aid, then perhaps I shall spare her a moment or two.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: ...After all, the flower, the star of the songs of praise, shall seem less radiant if the green leaves are not there to serve as its foil.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The following labor shall be little, but it is still a radiant shard. Yasnapati mine, record it down with a reverent heart, and use even this mote of shattered light to grace your mighty hymn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can talk about the less important stuff later, Sorush. Let's figure out how to disperse that purple mist first!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: "Less important," you say!? *sigh* ... Well, so be it.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Mihir's sinful form renders her unable to fulfill her duty, but the thorns remain. So long as I lend them some of my strength, it shall only take a brief moment to scatter this purple smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: As for the downward path, let us follow that wandering Khvarena we just saw.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if Sorush's so sure... Let's try getting closer then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right. If you feel uncomfortable, then hold your breath! Well, Paimon isn't all that good at doing that herself... so you'd better make it quick, Sorush!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Underestimate me not, Pale Floater.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. Aren't you allies? Are you really gonna leave a fellow Pari to her fate like that?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Stop making such disgraceful noises. Would I lead you wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Hmph. Pale Floater, you could stand to learn from our Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} unflinching calm.

choices.text: To be honest, I am somewhat nervous on the inside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Just looking at that big mass of... stuff over there is pretty scary already...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Such trivial trials! They pale in comparison to the sacrifice that I must offer up later.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ah, I misspeak. You, Pale Floater, are not as bold as my Yasnapati... But perhaps one may consider retreating at the slightest sign of danger a wise choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right... That's right! {NICKNAME}'s in charge of being brave, while Paimon's in charge of being smart. That's why we make the best of buddies, after all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nice going, buddy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, right? Paimon thinks that was a good rejoinder too!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ... But I did not give you your title for naught, Yasnapati. Do give praise unto my bravery more, pray.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}'s known Paimon longer. When {M#he's}{F#she's} not being your Yasnapati, there's nothing wrong with {M#him}{F#her} sparing some time to praise Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, don't sweat the small stuff, Sorush. You're not really doing anything that especially needs praising right now, are you...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: My great work is not for the present, but the future. Still, at this very moment... you are being given the privilege to witness where it all begins!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you say so. Speaking of which, we're here to find...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Mihir. That foolish familiar of thorns... She must be suffering right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. Is she trapped in there? Then we've got to go save her!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The power of the purple mist beneath us shares a source with the demons of Dev. Mihir's task should have been to keep such wicked powers from running rampant upon this earth.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Under the Sign of Apaosha, the powers of the two forces warring here ebb and flow...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: We Pari should be dauntless, willing to fight till we ourselves are torn to shreds... but Mihir? Hah. I shouldn't wonder if she searches for some way to protect herself even now, conducting some loathsome struggle.

choices.text: It is just a fluorescent purple mist.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But don't you find that pretty suspicious already? Paimon can tell how dangerous it is just by looking!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this Mihir? Is she... stuck? Seems like the purple mist has already made it all the way down here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do now, Sorush? Can we just do what we did earlier? Y'know, give some of your power to the thorns and free her?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Why of course, I shall save her. After all, she does seem so very piteous, infested with corruption and helpless as she is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This isn't the best time to throw shade on her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! We've got to save her, and quick...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Yet I have not heard her repent! I shall hear her repudiation of her obduracy and her supplication for my aid...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, are you serious? We don't have time for that kinda talk! Paimon thought you were just speaking in anger...

choices.text: O valiant, dauntless Lady Sorush, we implore thee!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop playing along with her!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Well, then... If you, too, say so, my Yasnapati. After all, fulfilling your wishes once in a while is indeed within the purview of one so exalted as I.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? Seriously? Paimon wishes you'd listen to her too, Sorush...

choices.text: Lovely, invincible Lady Sorush, shall ye not hear my counsel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure that's gonna work...?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose she is alive, if barely, and covered in sin, and weakened to the extent that she may only defend herself...

choices.text: All thanks to you, great Lady Sorush.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Sorush, Sorush... Sorush who took humans for companions. Sorush who lost her way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... It sounds like there's some secret meaning behind her words...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Do not get near her, lest the defilement that emanates from her touches you...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It seems that she has not only forgone a heart of gratitude, but has lost much of her intellect, or she would not use such baseless words to reproach me.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Thank you, Sorush. If not for you and your companions, I would have needed much time to gather my strength...

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: And even then, I am unsure if I could have stood against the rising filth on my own.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: The Sign of Apaosha could be seen all too clearly, even from the bottom of the valley, but thorns can only crawl upon the ground, never to reach the sky — not even the reflection of the skies on the earth...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. Of course. After all, I am the one who is destined to make sacrifices and extinguish the Sign.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #And I must add that {NICKNAME} is no companion of mine, nor is Paimon. {M#He}{F#She} is my Yasnapati, a willing instrument recording my great work.

choices.text: Sorush's number one Yasnapati, that's me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to be number one too! Uh, wait... Why would Paimon wanna fight you to be Sorush's "willing instrument," anyway?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm... Just saving Mihir isn't enough to complete what Zurvan asked us to do, right?

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: I see. So you have something to request of me, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: What? Have your senses gnarled into tumbleweed during your imprisonment and departed the Temir Mountains into the nameless dunes?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It is by my magnanimity in not remembering past slights that my Yasnapati has been given leave to record your name within the hymn that sings my praises.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Your sinful form, stained with defilement, should never otherwise have appeared within those stanzas...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You should thank me, Mihir. If it was not for our Elder... Ah, whatever. We do this to obtain the Twin-Horned Chaplet. For that reason, you must return with me to the Vourukasha Oasis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, Sorush... You keep talking about "stained with defilement" this and "sinful form" that... What do you even mean?

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: It is the duty of us familiars of the thorn to prevent defilement from spreading across the earth and guard against its corrosion. But when we battle against the demons of Dev, injury is nigh unavoidable.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: And if you had been shattered in battle with them, that might have been worth a song... But stained as you are, you can hardly be counted as one of us.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If it were not for my coming to your rescue, you would likely have continued some pathetic struggle here, till the world forgot you, and you utterly faded away.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Those are the words of the human who has befriended you, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: He is no ordinary human. He is the Nasuraia of the Order of Skeptics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so that's how it is...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like a matter of wounded pride.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Calling someone "sinful" because of that... Mihir, you poor thing!

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: To do one's duty is not a pitiable act. Nor is struggling to perform that duty for a while longer shameful.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Pah! Never mind the matter of our Elder. I have not fallen so low as to require your judgment! Rather, it is you who should thank me for rescuing you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh come on, Sorush, stop yelling at an injured person! Well... Mihir was wounded in combat, so that counts, right?

response.text: You plebeians miss the point. Back to the heart of the matter, we did disperse some purple mist, but their root cause remains unresolved. I doubt that she can hold out for much longer. How pitiful...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Pah, what a horrible sight. To be as Mihir is, corroded by filth, falling from a spotless to a sinful state, yet desperate to preserve herself... Had the Elder not bade me come...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. So after all that, you do care!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hardly! I merely wish to see if that useless fool has any regrets or not. If she turns back to us and accepts our aid, then perhaps I shall spare her a moment or two.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...After all, the flower, the star of the songs of praise, shall seem less radiant if the green leaves are not there to serve as its foil.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The following labor shall be little, but it is still a radiant shard. Yasnapati mine, record it down with a reverent heart, and use even this mote of shattered light to grace your mighty hymn.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can talk about the less important stuff later, Sorush. Let's figure out how to save Mihir first, shall we?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: "Less important," you say!? *sigh* ... Well, so be it.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Mihir's sinful form renders her unable to do her duty, but the thorns remain. So long as I lend them some of my strength, scattering this defilement should cost me but a little effort.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: As for the downward path, let us follow that wandering Khvarena we just saw.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if Sorush's so sure... Let's try getting closer then!

choices.text: You wouldn't be unable to rescue your comrade by any chance, would you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, maybe you're right. The problem could very well be something not even Sorush can solve.

choices.text: The Aranara all help each other out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! They're like a big family, always protecting one another! So you Pari aren't like that, huh...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The Aranara? Hah. What a carefree breed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, uh... Are you sure we're going the right way, Sorush? We seem to have been around these parts before...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Stop making such disgraceful noises. Would I lead you wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Hmph. Pale Floater, you could stand to learn from our Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} unflinching calm.

choices.text: To be honest, I am somewhat nervous on the inside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! This place still doesn't look safe at all, just like the last time we came here!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Such trivial trials! They pale in comparison to the sacrifice that I must offer up later.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ah, I misspeak. You, Pale Floater, are not as bold as my Yasnapati... But perhaps one may consider retreating at the slightest sign of danger a wise choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right... That's right! {NICKNAME}'s in charge of being brave, while Paimon's in charge of being smart. That's why we make the best of buddies, after all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nice going, buddy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, right? Paimon thinks that was a good rejoinder too!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ... But I did not give you your title for naught, Yasnapati. Do give praise unto my bravery more, pray.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}'s known Paimon longer. When {M#he's}{F#she's} not being your Yasnapati, there's nothing wrong with {M#him}{F#her} sparing some time to praise Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, don't sweat the small stuff, Sorush. You're not really doing anything that especially needs praising right now, are you...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: My great work is not for the present, but the future. Still, at this very moment... you are being given the privilege to witness where it all begins!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you say so. Speaking of which, we're here to find...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Mihir. That foolish familiar of thorns... She must be suffering right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Sorush, so the Pari you mentioned about was Mihir? Is she trapped down there? In that case, we've gotta go save her!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The power of the purple mist you witnessed previously and the demons of Dev stem from the same source. Mihir's task should have been to keep such wicked powers from running rampant upon this earth.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Under the Sign of Apaosha, the powers of the two forces warring here ebb and flow...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: We Pari should be dauntless, willing to fight till we ourselves are torn to shreds... but Mihir? Hah. I shouldn't wonder if she searches for some way to protect herself even now, conducting some loathsome struggle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. Aren't you allies? Are you really gonna leave a fellow Pari to her fate like that?

choices.text: It's just some persistent purple mist, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And how is that not annoying enough, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this Mihir? Is she... stuck? Seems like the purple mist has already made it all the way down here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do now, Sorush? Can we just do what we did earlier? Y'know, give some of your power to the thorns and free her?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Why of course, I shall save her. After all, she does seem so very piteous, infested with corruption and helpless as she is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This isn't the best time to throw shade on her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! We've got to save her, and quick...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Yet I have not heard her repent! I shall hear her repudiation of her obduracy and her supplication for my aid...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, are you serious? We don't have time for that kinda talk! Paimon thought you were just speaking in anger...

choices.text: O valiant, dauntless Lady Sorush, we implore thee!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop playing along with her!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Well, then... If you, too, say so, my Yasnapati. After all, fulfilling your wishes once in a while is indeed within the purview of one so exalted as I.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? Seriously? Paimon wishes you'd listen to her too, Sorush...

choices.text: Lovely, invincible Lady Sorush, shall ye not hear my counsel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure that's gonna work...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Are you alright, Mihir?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose she is alive, if barely, and covered in sin, and weakened to the extent that she may only defend herself...

choices.text: All thanks to you, great Lady Sorush.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Sorush, Sorush... Sorush who took humans for companions. Sorush who lost her way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... It sounds like there's some secret meaning behind her words...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Do not get near her, lest the defilement that emanates from her touches you...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It seems that she has not only forgone a heart of gratitude, but has lost much of her intellect, or she would not use such baseless words to reproach me.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Thank you, Sorush. If not for you and your companions, I would have needed much time to gather my strength...

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: And even then, I am unsure if I could have stood against the rising filth on my own.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: The Sign of Apaosha could be seen all too clearly, even from the bottom of the valley, but thorns can only crawl upon the ground, never to reach the sky — not even the reflection of the skies on the earth...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. Of course. After all, I am the one who is destined to make sacrifices and extinguish the Sign.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #And I must add that {NICKNAME} is no companion of mine, nor is Paimon. {M#He}{F#She} is my Yasnapati, a willing instrument recording my great work.

choices.text: Sorush's number one Yasnapati, that's me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to be number one too! Uh, wait... Why would Paimon wanna fight you to be Sorush's "willing instrument," anyway?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm... Just saving Mihir isn't enough to complete what Zurvan asked us to do, right?

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: I see. So you have something to request of me, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: What? Have your senses gnarled into tumbleweed during your imprisonment and departed the Temir Mountains into the nameless dunes?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It is by my magnanimity in not remembering past slights that my Yasnapati has been given leave to record your name within the hymn that sings my praises.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Your sinful form, stained with defilement, should never otherwise have appeared within those stanzas...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You should thank me, Mihir. If it was not for our Elder... Ah, whatever. We do this to obtain the Twin-Horned Chaplet. For that reason, you must return with me to the Vourukasha Oasis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, Sorush... You keep talking about "stained with defilement" this and "sinful form" that... What do you even mean?

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: It is the duty of us familiars of the thorn to prevent defilement from spreading across the earth and guard against its corrosion. But when we battle against the demons of Dev, injury is nigh unavoidable.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: And if you had been shattered in battle with them, that might have been worth a song... But stained as you are, you can hardly be counted as one of us.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If it were not for my coming to your rescue, you would likely have continued some pathetic struggle here, till the world forgot you, and you utterly faded away.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: Those are the words of the human who has befriended you, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: He is no ordinary human. He is the Nasu{RUBY#[S]Vijnanapati}raia of the Order of Skeptics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so that's how it is...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like a matter of wounded pride.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Calling someone "sinful" because of that... Mihir, you poor thing!

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: To do one's duty is not a pitiable act. Nor is struggling to perform that duty for a while longer shameful.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Pah! Never mind the matter of our Elder. I have not fallen so low as to require your judgment! Rather, it is you who should thank me for rescuing you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh come on, Sorush, stop yelling at an injured person! Well... Mihir was wounded in combat, so that counts, right?

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: It is alright. Sorush... will understand, or she will never obtain the Twin-Horned Chaplet from Zurvan.

response.speaker: Mihir
response.text: But as she says, my "sinful" form is unacceptable in the eyes of other Pari. I cannot return to the Vourukasha Oasis in this state...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Merely perform a cleansing pilgrimage, and it will be well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A cleansing pilgrimage? Will that take a long time? Will it be dangerous?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You need not be so concerned as to the details of Mihir's deeds. After all, there shall be little room for her in the praises that shall be sung of me.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: She knows this road well, but in her weak and helpless state, were she to be attacked along the way, I doubt there will be anything left of her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, what Paimon's hearing is that things will be fine as long as we escort her. Don't worry, we're very experienced at this sorta thing!

choices.text: I would call that description a few degrees off reality.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're companions, aren't we?

choices.text: Good thing we arrived early, and had you with us, Sorush.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back! Guess your cleansing pilgrimage is done, huh, Mihir? And that means your "defilement" issues have been solved, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: The Vourukasha Oasis has wonderful winds and waters, and bountiful energies...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, this place sure is better than that valley full of purple mist. It's definitely got that... "soul-purifying" feeling to it.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Purification...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that all? Well, that was easier than Paimon thought! Now that Mihir's clear of this "defilement," other Pari aren't gonna reject her anymore, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can finally take a rest after all that trouble you went through, Mihir.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And Sorush is now closer to obtaining the Chaplet as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Everyone wins!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: A fitting end for Mihir, perhaps, but not for me.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My ending will not be something so ordinary or peaceful... or as insignificant as you are, Pale Floater.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon isn't insignificant! ... Well, not that Paimon's very heavy or anything either!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My end shall be glorious, radiant, like that of the divine bird Simurgh. I shall split into infinite motes of Khvarena, cleansing the world of its impurity...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That which Mihir has done cannot be compared to what I shall yet accomplish.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Yet there was only one Simurgh, and there is only one Sorush.

choices.text: There's no need to imitate others.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: My Yasnapati, it is clear that you do not understand Simurgh's greatness. Nor do you rate the tragic vow and resolve of us Pari as you should.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You speak but empty words, born of your witlessness. My mind is made up, my heart set. I will not be moved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon doesn't get Sorush at all. Why does she insist on sacrificing herself to deal with the Sign? And why is she so cold to Mihir?

choices.text: Well, the way things look right now, Mihir's the one with deeds to her name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what you're saying is that Sorush hasn't done anything yet? Hmm, if you think about it, Mihir has been doing her best to protect the land from corruption, but Sorush...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd say she's pretty anxious about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon kinda gets it now! Sorush's worried that if we praise Mihir, we won't do the same for her afterward, so she wants to do something even greater...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, come on! Isn't she just afraid that Mihir will steal her Yasnapati?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #She doesn't need to worry about that. We're born flatterers, aren't we, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon think... Let's put four lines of praise for Sorush in that hymn or whatever she's always going on about, and two for Mihir. That way, everyone wins! Hehe.

choices.text: It's because Sorush's work is not yet complete.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. We don't know if we'll be able to obtain the Twin-Horned Chaplet yet, never mind extinguish the Sign of Apaosha... So she's worried that she's falling behind Mihir?

choices.text: There has to be a way that doesn't involve sacrifice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks so too! You don't have to be in such a hurry to sacrifice yourself! We can think of something else together!

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: I will not require a Yasnapati. Sorush may desire human praise, but I do not need it.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Still, I'm grateful for this chance to return to the Vourukasha Oasis for a brief respite. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of that, why didn't you help Mihir earlier, Sorush?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you just lent a little power to the thorns, you could've done that even without our help, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: This is my duty, not hers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But shouldn't you help each other out at times like this?

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Each Pari has their own mission, and just like this cleansing pilgrimage, we must undertake those tasks ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Missions and duties... all have someone they belong to, and we cannot allow others to take over completely.
